title: fix(plugin-security): the unowned permission-set refusal moves a counter
body:
Fixes #18571

Clause-②: yes (widening)

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-18571-unowned-refusal-counter`

## What was wrong

The permission-set seeder's unowned refusal moved no counter, while every sibling refusal on both seeder axes moved one.

`bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts` `upsertPackagePermissionSet` refuses to materialize a declared set whose owner cannot be resolved (`!packageId`): an unowned `managed_by:'package'` row makes uninstall undefined, which is the ADR-0086 D3 ambiguity the branch exists to prevent. #18564 gave that refusal an author-visible line. What it left behind is the programmatic half — the branch returned an outcome with all six counters at `0`, so a caller that reads no log at all (a boot report, a Setup surface, a test) could not tell a pass that refused a declaration from a pass with nothing to do. The branch's own comment said so verbatim: 「this branch moves no counter either, so the outcome said nothing about it」.

The asymmetry is measured, not cited. The sibling axis (`bootstrap-declared-capabilities.ts`) has carried `skippedUnowned` since #4967 and increments it at the same ADR-0086 D3 boundary.

Re-verified on `origin/main` before writing, against the three commits that landed on this file pair after the card was filed — `cf39b83c` (#18564), `f9e16d85` (#19411), `8f6d8314` (#19437). None of them changed the picture; the defect was live at `fbc12be3`.

## What changed

`PermissionSeedOutcome` gains a **required** `skippedUnowned: number`, incremented on the `!packageId` branch.

Required, like `skippedForeign` and unlike the optional `deleted`: an absent key on a *refusal* count reads exactly like a pass with nothing to refuse, which is the defect restated.

Four construction sites, all in-repo, all initialized:

| site | before | after |
|:---|:---|:---|
| `bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts:232` (`upsertPackagePermissionSet`) | `{ seeded, updated, unchanged, unreadable, skippedEnvAuthored, skippedForeign }` | `+ skippedUnowned: 0` |
| `bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts:377` (`bootstrapDeclaredPermissions`) | same six | `+ skippedUnowned: 0` |
| `permission-set-projection.ts:569` (`upsertEnvPermissionSet`) | same six | `+ skippedUnowned: 0` |
| `permission-set-projection.ts:752` (`retirePermissionSetRecord`) | same six `+ deleted: 0` | `+ skippedUnowned: 0` |

The boot aggregator forwards it alongside the five counters it already carried. The branch's stale comment — the one that stated the defect — is corrected rather than left lying.

⛔ **The refusal itself is unchanged**, and no other diagnostic, log line or field was added. This adds a channel, not a verdict.

## Tests

Four cases in `bootstrap-declared-permissions.test.ts`, modelled on the capability axis' instrument:

- `BOOT-LOOP DOOR: an unowned declaration increments skippedUnowned` — and lands in its own counter, with `skippedForeign` / `skippedEnvAuthored` / `unreadable` all still `0`.
- `PUBLISH DOOR (ADR-0086 P2): the materializer increments it too` — that caller passes no collector and aggregates nothing, so a fix wired into the boot loop alone would have left it exactly as silent as before. Testing one door is testing half.
- `CONTROL: a pass that refuses nothing leaves it at 0 through both doors` — the discriminating half; without it a counter incremented on every declaration satisfies both assertions above.
- `⭐ CONSERVATION: every named declaration lands in exactly one counter` — six declarations, one per counter, summed over **every** counter the outcome declares rather than a hand-picked subset, so a future counter with no home here fails this pin instead of hiding. That is the failure mode `skippedUnowned` itself was.

No existing assertion was weakened or deleted, and none broke: the outcome is read with `toMatchObject` and per-field `expect` throughout, never `toEqual` / `toStrictEqual`.

## The fence this round was told to stop at, and why it did not

Triage attached a stop condition verbatim: 「承接席若发现该类型是跨包公开导出且有外部消费者,那一刻回来找维护者,⛔ 不自行扩面」.

The first half is true — `PermissionSeedOutcome` is barrel-exported at `index.ts:125` and re-exported at `bootstrap-declared-permissions.ts:85`. So the second half was measured: **does anything CONSTRUCT one outside `packages/plugins/plugin-security/`?** Reading one is harmless; constructing one is what a required field breaks.

- **This repo, whole-tree sweep:** every occurrence of the type name and of the distinctive member `skippedEnvAuthored` is inside `packages/plugins/plugin-security/`. The only cross-file consumer, `security-plugin.ts:3759`, *reads* `r.skippedEnvAuthored` — no construction. No other in-repo package re-exports the type.
- **`objectui` (pinned sibling):** no dependency on `@objectstack/plugin-security`, and no occurrence of the type. Its hits are prose about the plugin's FLS middleware.
- **Downstream app repos checked out here (`duly`, `hotcrm`, `objectos`):** only `hotcrm` depends on the package (`17.4.0`); it imports `SecurityPlugin`, `PermissionEvaluator`, `appDefaultPermissionSetName` and `buildContextForUser` in six tests and never names the outcome type. `duly` and `objectos` do not depend on it at all.

Zero external constructors found on every surface reachable from here, so the field is required as the card and triage both asked. The residual is named rather than papered over: the package publishes to npm, so an unreachable consumer cannot be excluded by a sweep — what can be said is that nothing in any checkout available to this round constructs one.

## Acceptance notes

Noted, not filed:

- `security-plugin.ts:3754-3761` picks the publish materializer's failure reason by elimination: `skippedForeign`, else `skippedEnvAuthored`, else the unowned wording as the fallback arm. With `skippedUnowned` now on the outcome that last arm could name its own counter instead of being reached by exhaustion. Behaviour is identical either way and the current wording is correct, so this is a legibility preference, not a defect — and the card's fence says a channel, nothing else. Carrier: the next PR that touches this publish branch.
- `permission-set-projection.ts` documents the permission-set accounting identity only in the new member's docblock, while the capability axis states its identity on `materializedNames`. Both are correct and neither is wrong; consolidating them is a prose-shape preference, not a defect. Carrier: none — no PR or person is queued to touch this docblock.

## Local verification

See the dev report comment on #18571 for the gate families, their exit codes and the `check-widening-tells` invocation.
